newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: UAE oil minister sees stronger crude prices.
newsitem.headline: UAE oil minister sees stronger crude prices.

text.p: The United Arab Emirates'(UAE) oil minister on Saturday said world crude prices could climb to the $19-20 a barrel range late this year.

"World markets have overcome recent weakness and prices should consolidate after a seasonal decline due to diminishing demand," said Obaid bin Saif al-Nasseri, UAE's Petroleum and Mineral Resources Minister.
"Prices in the fourth quarter will regain their previous levels," said Nasseri, who was speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the Information Revolution in Financial Markets conference.
"We hope prices will be in the $19-20 range," he added.
Oil prices fell from over $24 at the start of the year to under $18 in April.
The UAE, with an Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) supply quota of 2.161 million barrels per day, derives about 75 percent of government revenue from oil.
The UAE, one of the few oil producers with spare production capacity and reserves of crude to last a century, has an estimated annual oil income of $9 billion.
